heroHeadline: FDA's Post-Closure Letter to Produce Industry Restates Existing Law, Marler Says — Root Cause of Record Outbreak Still Unnamed
heroSubtitle: Two days after CDC and FDA declared the multistate Cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms de México iceberg lettuce over at 12,883 illnesses, 570 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths across 21 states, FDA published a letter calling on every link in the produce supply chain to review Cyclospora prevention practices. Food-safety attorney Bill Marler, writing Sept 13, said the letter's cited obligations — water management, worker hygiene, sanitation, and supplier verification — are 'already the law,' and that FDA has still not named how the parasite reached the lettuce in sufficient quantity to sicken nearly 13,000 people. He proposed ten concrete steps FDA could take instead, including publishing investigation findings, funding a grower-level detection method, and restoring parasite research funding cut in recent years. FDA's root-cause investigation at the Taylor Farms de México facility remains open with no stated timeline.
